metadata.name: Atrial fibrillation
metadata.emergency_level: Usually routine - but AF with haemodynamic instability or acute stroke is an emergency
metadata.severity: Ranges from asymptomatic to disabling; main harm is stroke risk

overview.short_description: The commonest sustained cardiac arrhythmia, an irregularly irregular atrial rhythm causing palpitations, breathlessness and fatigue, whose greatest danger is a markedly increased risk of stroke.
overview.detailed_description: Atrial fibrillation is common and increases with age. It may be paroxysmal, persistent or permanent, and is often found incidentally (including asymptomatic). Diagnosis requires an ECG (or ambulatory monitoring). Management has three strands: STROKE PREVENTION with anticoagulation guided by risk score (the priority), RATE or RHYTHM control for symptoms, and treatment of underlying causes/precipitants.
overview.pathophysiology: Disorganised atrial electrical activity replaces coordinated contraction, causing an irregular ventricular response; loss of atrial 'kick' and stasis (especially the left atrial appendage) promotes thrombus formation and embolic stroke.
overview.etiology: Hypertension, ischaemic/valvular/structural heart disease, heart failure, hyperthyroidism, alcohol, sepsis/infection, pulmonary disease/PE, obesity and sleep apnoea; often multifactorial or 'lone' AF.
overview.natural_history: Often progresses from paroxysmal to persistent/permanent; embolic and heart-failure risk if untreated.
overview.prognosis: Good with appropriate anticoagulation and rate/rhythm control; untreated AF carries substantial stroke and heart-failure risk.

prevalence.value: The most common sustained arrhythmia; prevalence rises steeply with age (several percent of older adults).

incidence.value: Increases with age and cardiovascular disease.

mortality.value: Increased mortality mainly via stroke and heart failure.

epidemiology.sex_predominance: Slightly more common in men; strokes from AF often more severe in women.

risk_factors.lifestyle: Excess alcohol ('holiday heart'), obesity, physical inactivity; also endurance athletes.
risk_factors.alcohol: Acute and chronic excess precipitate AF.
risk_factors.obesity: Strong risk factor (and via sleep apnoea).
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Hypertension, heart failure, coronary/valvular disease, hyperthyroidism, obstructive sleep apnoea, chronic lung disease.

chief_complaints.importance: Often found on examination/opportunistic pulse check

symptoms.importance: Common but AF can be asymptomatic

symptoms.symptom: Chest pain, syncope, or acute severe breathlessness (with fast AF)
symptoms.importance: RED FLAG - haemodynamic compromise / precipitated ischaemia/heart failure

negative_findings.finding: Regular pulse and normal ECG at the time
negative_findings.why_important: AF unlikely at that moment (but paroxysmal AF needs ambulatory monitoring to capture)

negative_findings.finding: No structural heart disease, normal thyroid, no precipitant
negative_findings.why_important: Suggests 'lone'/idiopathic AF; still assess stroke risk

history_questions.question: Do you feel an irregular fast heartbeat, and is it constant or does it come and go?
history_questions.why_ask: Distinguishes paroxysmal from persistent; guides monitoring

history_questions.question: Any chest pain, blackouts, or severe breathlessness with episodes?
Stroke risk factors (age, hypertension, diabetes, prior stroke/TIA, heart failure, vascular disease)?
Bleeding risk factors and current medications (including alcohol)?
Any thyroid symptoms, alcohol excess, or recent infection?

physical_examination.examination: Blood pressure and signs of haemodynamic compromise
Cardiac and respiratory exam (heart failure, valve disease)

vital_signs.heart_rate: Often raised and irregular; may be very fast
vital_signs.blood_pressure: Variable; low BP with fast AF suggests compromise

laboratory_tests.test_name: Thyroid function tests, U&E, FBC, glucose
laboratory_tests.indication: Identify precipitants and baseline for treatment

laboratory_tests.test_name: Renal/liver function and FBC (for anticoagulant choice/dosing)

imaging.when_needed: Assess structural/valvular disease, LV function, and to guide rhythm-control/anticoagulation decisions
imaging.expected_findings: Valve disease, LV dysfunction, atrial enlargement

ecg.when_needed: REQUIRED to diagnose - 12-lead ECG (and ambulatory/patch monitoring for paroxysmal AF)
ecg.findings: Irregularly irregular rhythm with ABSENT P waves and a fibrillatory baseline; variable ventricular rate.

other_diagnostic_tests.ambulatory_monitoring: Holter/patch/implantable monitors to capture paroxysmal AF

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: ECG demonstration of atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm with absent distinct P waves (fibrillatory waves), lasting at least 30 seconds on a rhythm strip/single-lead. Classify as paroxysmal, persistent, long-standing persistent, or permanent. Then assess STROKE RISK (CHA2DS2-VASc) and bleeding risk (e.g., ORBIT/HAS-BLED to identify modifiable factors).

diagnostic_scores.value: CHA2DS2-VASc for stroke risk; bleeding-risk tools (e.g., ORBIT/HAS-BLED) to address modifiable bleeding factors (not to withhold anticoagulation).

cutoff_values.value: Offer anticoagulation based on CHA2DS2-VASc (e.g., consider at score >=1 in men / >=2 in women; offer at >=2). Do not use bleeding risk alone to withhold anticoagulation.

differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is the rhythm regular with sawtooth waves on ECG?

differential_diagnosis.differences: ECG pattern differs (regular SVT; discrete ectopics)
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Do episodes start and stop suddenly and look regular on ECG?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Sinus tachycardia (e.g., from sepsis, anaemia, PE, thyrotoxicosis)
differential_diagnosis.differences: Regular with normal P waves; underlying cause
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is the rhythm regular with a clear precipitant?

differential_diagnosis.disease: AF causing/with acute complications (stroke, heart failure, ischaemia)
differential_diagnosis.red_flags: Focal neurology, pulmonary oedema, chest pain
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any stroke symptoms, severe breathlessness, or chest pain?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you haemodynamically compromised now (chest pain, severe breathlessness, syncope, low BP)?
What is the CHA2DS2-VASc score (stroke risk factors)?

next_best_question.question: Are you stable, what is your stroke risk (CHA2DS2-VASc) and bleeding risk, and are you very symptomatic?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Unstable -> emergency; stable -> anticoagulate per stroke risk + rate control (or rhythm control if symptomatic/appropriate) + treat cause

next_best_test.why: Find cause and guide anticoagulation/rhythm decisions

red_flags.finding: AF with haemodynamic instability (hypotension, severe breathlessness/pulmonary oedema, chest pain, syncope)
red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency - urgent assessment; consider emergency electrical cardioversion

red_flags.finding: Very fast ventricular rate with ischaemia or heart failure
New AF - assess stroke risk urgently
red_flags.immediate_action: Do not overlook anticoagulation (the main preventable harm)

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Unstable AF (emergency); AF with stroke/TIA (emergency); AF causing heart failure/ischaemia.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Rhythm-control consideration (young/symptomatic/refractory), consideration of cardioversion/ablation, or diagnostic uncertainty.

early: Rapid ventricular response with heart failure/ischaemia
late: Heart failure (tachycardia-induced or via lost atrial contraction)

initial_management.supportive_care: Confirm on ECG; assess stability; identify and treat precipitants/causes (thyroid, alcohol, infection, sleep apnoea); educate about stroke prevention.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Direct-acting oral anticoagulant; Vitamin K antagonist; Beta-blocker; Diltiazem/verapamil. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG196.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Reduce alcohol, weight loss, treat sleep apnoea and hypertension, physical activity.
initial_management.follow_up: Review symptoms, rate/rhythm control, anticoagulation adherence and bleeding, and renal function; reassess stroke risk over time.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: STROKE PREVENTION is the priority: offer anticoagulation (a direct oral anticoagulant first-line, or warfarin) based on CHA2DS2-VASc; do not use aspirin for stroke prevention in AF; address modifiable bleeding factors rather than withholding anticoagulation. RATE control first-line for most: beta-blocker or rate-limiting calcium-channel blocker (digoxin as an option, e.g., sedentary/heart failure). RHYTHM control (cardioversion, antiarrhythmics, ablation) for those symptomatic despite rate control, newer/reversible AF, or heart failure. Emergency cardioversion if haemodynamically unstable.

patient_education.home_advice: Atrial fibrillation is an irregular heartbeat. It can cause palpitations, breathlessness and tiredness, but its most important risk is stroke - which is why blood-thinning (anticoagulant) medication is usually the key treatment; take it exactly as prescribed and report any unusual bleeding. Other medicines control your heart rate. Reducing alcohol, losing weight and treating sleep apnoea help. Get emergency help for stroke symptoms (face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty), severe breathlessness, chest pain, or blackouts.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: الرجفان الأذيني نظم قلب غير منتظم. قد يسبّب خفقاناً وضيق نفس وتعباً، لكن أخطر ما فيه هو خطر الجلطة الدماغية - ولذلك يكون دواء تمييع الدم (المضاد للتخثّر) هو العلاج الأهم عادةً؛ تناوله تماماً كما وُصف وأبلغ عن أي نزيف غير معتاد. وأدوية أخرى تضبط سرعة القلب. يفيد تقليل الكحول وإنقاص الوزن وعلاج انقطاع النفس النومي. اطلب المساعدة الطارئة عند أعراض الجلطة (تدلّي الوجه، ضعف الذراع، صعوبة الكلام)، أو ضيق نفس شديد، أو ألم صدر، أو إغماء.
patient_education.prevention: Manage hypertension, weight, alcohol and sleep apnoea; anticoagulation prevents strokes in those at risk.
patient_education.warning_signs: Stroke symptoms (FAST), severe breathlessness, chest pain, blackout, or unusual bleeding on anticoagulants.

prevention.lifestyle: Weight loss, alcohol reduction, treating hypertension and sleep apnoea reduce AF burden.
prevention.screening: Opportunistic pulse checks/ECG in older adults to detect AF (case-finding).

evidence.evidence_level: High - strong evidence that anticoagulation prevents AF-related stroke; established rate/rhythm strategies.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG196; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
evidence.legacy_guideline_strength_pre_v13: Strong - NICE NG196, ESC atrial fibrillation guidelines.
